graph/description: **A short memory.** The air clears about a ninth of its methane every year, so methane answers a change in emissions within a decade, unlike CO₂, which lingers for centuries. With emissions held at today's $E$, it levels off at the steady state $M^{*} = E\tau / 2.75$, approached as $M(t) = M^{*} + (M_0 - M^{*})\,e^{-t/\tau}$. Three futures from today's emissions: held, cut 30% by 2030 (the size of the Global Methane Pledge), and rising 1% a year. The right axis is the warming push (radiative forcing) methane exerts. **Hover** a year.
graph/name: A short memory: three futures from today's emissions
